I am always a bit hesitent of hypervisors just because I am not terribly good at security and I do have to ssh into the machine. Thanks though, I will check it out.

Xen is not actually a linux. The hypervisor or xen is a micro OS that can't do anything other than host virtual machines. It can't even do a lot with the file system so it needs one guest called dom0 that has privileges to do administration and the level of programming to get it done.

This actually shows how cool debian is. You aren't really installing xen to run in your debian as a visualization program. You are actually installing a new main OS on your computer (xen) and configuring your current os as dom0 (which is a guest). The actual installed software on the system is equivalent to guest additions on virtualbox.

If you have Ulcerative Colitis (autoimmune disease that causes ulcers in your large intestine) it's best to see a doctor and determine a schedule for how often you should get a colonoscopy. This is imperative as Ulcerative Colitis increases your chances of colon cancer & should be watched for accordingly.
